t: This is St James Garlickhythe, a Church of England parish church in the Vintry ward of the City. Look up at its many windows and you'll see why people nickname it Wren's lantern. Christopher Wren designed it, as part of the rebuilding of fifty-two City churches that followed the Great Fire of 1666. Buried here is James Jurin, a doctor and mathematician, remembered for early work on capillary action and on smallpox vaccination. He was also a keen defender of Isaac Newton, often using satire on his behalf.
